recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not reintroduce Provenance.entity.type or add redundant Provenance prose for FHIR-7460; future work should use the current Provenance.entity.what and Reference.identifier model, with any broader design change handled as a new Security/Infrastructure issue.
issue_request: FHIR-7460 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the 2015 May ballot and asked to change Provenance.entity.type from a Required binding to resource-types to an extensible binding so Provenance could identify entities whose source content is not a FHIR resource.
initial_application: No exact FHIR-7460-tagged git commit was found because the Jira comment says the tooling-error fix was pre-applied in SVN. The DSTU2 source import already shows ProvenanceEntityType bound to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/resource-types with Conformance = extensible, demonstrating that the requested binding correction had already been applied historically.
additional_context: Provenance is active in source/fhir.ini. Later Published issue FHIR-9996 changed the Provenance model by disabling Provenance.entity.type and Provenance.entity.display, changing entity identity to a Reference(Any)-style element, and adding import/transform guidance for HL7 v2/CDA-derived content. Current source defines Provenance.entity.role, Provenance.entity.what, and Provenance.entity.agent; entity.what says what.identifier should be used for entities that are not a Resource type, and Reference guidance documents identifier logical references for cases where no FHIR representation exists when the reference type is Reference(Any).
reconciliation: No source change was made. The obsolete Required binding was historically made extensible and then superseded by the current Provenance.entity.what/Reference design, so there is no active Provenance.entity.type/resource-types binding to correct.

related_jiras.note: Another Published 2015 May Provenance issue requested the same Required-to-extensible resource-types binding change and is already represented on the combined branch by a no-change audit.

A later Published DSTU2 Provenance issue removed Provenance.entity.type/display and changed entity identity to Reference(Any), superseding the old discriminator while preserving non-FHIR import/transform use cases.
A later AuditEvent issue removed AuditEvent.entity.type as redundant with entity.what, consistent with the broader move away from separate entity type discriminators.
A later Applied technical correction updated the current Provenance.entity.what comment to say what.identifier is used for entities that are not a Resource type.
